newsitem.title: PERU: Rio Algom, Inmet plan $13.5 mln Peru investment.
newsitem.headline: Rio Algom, Inmet plan $13.5 mln Peru investment.

text.p: The Canadian consortium of Rio Algom Ltd and Inmet Mining Corp plans to invest at least $13.5 million on exploration at Peru's Antamina prospect in the next two years, the government said Tuesday.

An Energy and Mines Ministry statement said this money would be used "to complete the exploration tasks that allow them to prove with greater breadth and precision the level of proven and probable reserves which have been estimated at 130 million tonnes."
The Canadian companies bought the mainly copper-rich Antamina prospect from the state in July for a $20 million purchase price.

"If the result of the evaluations at the end of the two years is positive, and the group decides to continue with the Antamina prospect, they will have to assume the investment commitment of $2.52 billion in a period of five years," the statement said.
On September 6, Rio Algom and Inmet formally set up the Minera Antamina S.A. company, with a 50 percent stake each, to oversee the project.
The ministry said drilling work had begun at Antamina, in the northern Ancash region, and the aim of reaching a depth of 60,000 meters should be achieved within nine to 10 months.
In addition to the proven and probable reserves, the site has an estimated 900 million tonnes of potential reserves of copper, zinc, silver and molybdenum, the ministry added.
The Antamina prospect was sold as part of the government's piecemeal sell-off of state miner Centromin's assets.
